title: Hullbreaker Horror + Sol Ring + a two-mana rock: the real loop?

stack.note: cast for {2}; Hullbreaker Horror's cast trigger will go on the stack above it

extras.context: Stack 001 (checker: pass) refuted the two-card Hullbreaker Horror + Sol Ring infinite: the cast trigger locks its mode and target while the cast artifact is still a spell. The open question it left: with a THIRD recastable artifact — this deck runs Arcane Signet and Thought Vessel (and ran Fellwar Stone at the time of this resolution; benched 2026-07-28) — can the triggers alternate bounces so that each cast returns the OTHER artifact, and if so, is the resulting loop mana-neutral or mana-negative per full cycle, and does it produce an unbounded storm/cast count? Sapphire Medallion and Pearl Medallion are also in the 99 but NOT on this board — resolve the base three-card case first, then state (without a full walkthrough) what one Medallion changes.

scenario.question: With Hullbreaker Horror and Sol Ring on the battlefield and Arcane Signet being cast: walk the trigger choices and resolutions precisely. Can you sequence casts so that Arcane Signet's cast bounces Sol Ring and Sol Ring's re-cast bounces Arcane Signet, repeating? Account for every mana spent and produced in one full cycle: is the cycle mana-positive, mana-neutral, or mana-negative, and therefore is the cast/storm count unbounded with these three cards plus lands alone? State exactly what a Sapphire Medallion on the battlefield would change about the cycle's mana arithmetic.

steps.action: Casting Arcane Signet triggers Hullbreaker Horror ('Whenever you cast a spell, choose up to one — ... Return target nonland permanent to its owner's hand.'). The trigger goes on the stack above the Arcane Signet spell; its mode AND target are locked in now. Choose the second mode and target Sol Ring.
steps.effect: This is the exact point where the two-card version (stack 001) failed: the cast artifact is still a spell you control, so it is neither a legal target for 'target spell you don't control' nor a permanent. Sol Ring, however, is on the battlefield — it IS a nonland permanent — so it is a fully legal target here.

steps.action: With the trigger on the stack and Sol Ring still on the battlefield, you (holding priority or when you receive it) tap Sol Ring for mana: '{T}: Add {C}{C}.'
steps.effect: This is a mana ability — it does not use the stack and resolves immediately, so nothing can stop it. {C}{C} is now floating in your mana pool. Tapping Sol Ring before the bounce resolves is mandatory sequencing for the loop's mana math.

An activated mana ability doesn’t go on the stack, so it can’t be targeted, countered, or otherwise responded to. Rather, it resolves immediately after it is activated.

steps.action: The Hullbreaker Horror trigger (top of stack) resolves. Sol Ring is checked for target legality: it is still on the battlefield (tapped is irrelevant), so it is still legal. Sol Ring is returned to your hand.
steps.effect: Sol Ring is in your hand; the {C}{C} it made remains in your pool.

steps.action: With the stack now empty in your main phase, cast Sol Ring from your hand for {1}, paying with one floating {C} (one {C} remains floating). Hullbreaker Horror triggers again; choose 'Return target nonland permanent' targeting Arcane Signet — which is now a permanent on the battlefield, not a spell.
steps.effect: Note the timing constraint: artifacts are sorcery-speed, so the two casts cannot respond to each other — each cast must wait for the stack to empty. That is exactly why the bounces must ALTERNATE between two rocks rather than a rock bouncing itself. The trigger goes on the stack above the Sol Ring spell with Arcane Signet locked as its target.

steps.action: With the trigger on the stack, tap Arcane Signet for one mana of your commander's color identity — Heliod, the Radiant Dawn is white/blue, so {W} or {U} (either works; the loop only needs it as generic mana).
steps.effect: Legal even though the Signet just entered: the 'summoning sickness' tap restriction applies only to creatures, and Arcane Signet is a noncreature artifact. Floating mana is now {C} plus one {W} or {U}.

steps.action: The trigger resolves (Arcane Signet still on the battlefield, still a legal target): Arcane Signet returns to your hand. Then the Sol Ring spell resolves and enters the battlefield untapped.
steps.effect: The game state now exactly matches the cycle's start: Hullbreaker Horror and untapped Sol Ring on the battlefield, the two-mana rock in hand, you holding priority in your main phase with an empty stack. The loop is closed.

When all players pass in succession, the top (last-added) spell or ability on the stack resolves.

steps.action: Full-cycle mana ledger (one cycle = cast Signet, bounce+tap Sol Ring, cast Sol Ring, bounce+tap Signet).
steps.effect: Spent: {2} (Arcane Signet) + {1} (Sol Ring) = 3 mana. Produced: {C}{C} (Sol Ring) + 1 (Signet) = 3 mana. The cycle is exactly MANA-NEUTRAL. The 2 mana floating at the end of each cycle ({C} + {W/U}) pays the next cycle's Signet cost of {2}, so after the initial {2} investment (the {U}{U} available here) no further outside mana is ever needed.

citations.quote: When an effect instructs a player to add mana, that mana goes into a player’s mana pool. From there, it can be used to pay costs immediately, or it can stay in the player’s mana pool as unspent mana.

steps.action: Because each mana-neutral cycle returns to an identical game state with you holding priority, you may shortcut the loop for any chosen number of iterations: the cast/storm count IS unbounded with Hullbreaker Horror + Sol Ring + Arcane Signet plus {2} of starting mana. Substitutions for the two-mana rock: Thought Vessel substitutes exactly ({2} to cast, '{T}: Add {C}' — the same 3-spent/3-produced neutral ledger). Fellwar Stone substitutes only while an opponent controls a land that produces a color ('{T}: Add one mana of any color that a land an opponent controls could produce') — true in most real games, but false on this stated board, where both opponents' boards are empty: there Fellwar Stone taps for nothing and its cycle is mana-negative (3 spent, 2 produced), so the loop is NOT unbounded with it.
steps.effect: Precise bounds, stated exactly: (1) the loop nets ZERO mana, zero cards, and zero damage — it is a pure cast-count engine (2 casts per cycle), so it only wins through a payoff that cares about casts (e.g., a storm or magecraft-style effect) or by generating unbounded Hullbreaker triggers; (2) every trigger in the loop is consumed bouncing your own rock — the moment you aim a trigger at an opponent's permanent instead, the chain breaks (your rock stays on the battlefield and cannot be recast); (3) the loop lives inside a single phase, since the pool empties at end of phase — but arbitrarily many iterations fit before that, so this does not bound the count.

citations.quote: Occasionally the game gets into a state in which a set of actions could be repeated indefinitely (thus creating a “loop”). In that case, the shortcut rules can be used to determine how many times those actions are repeated without having to actually perform them

the player with priority may suggest a shortcut by describing a sequence of game choices, for all players, that may be legally taken based on the current game state and the predictable results of the sequence of choices
Each player’s mana pool empties at the end of each step and phase

steps.action: What Sapphire Medallion changes: nothing about this cycle's arithmetic. Its text is 'Blue spells you cast cost {1} less to cast' — but Sol Ring ({1}) and Arcane Signet ({2}) have no colored mana symbols in their mana costs, so both are colorless, and colorless is not a color. Neither cast in the cycle is a blue spell.
steps.effect: The Medallion discounts ZERO of the loop's casts: the cycle stays exactly mana-neutral and does NOT become mana-positive — no infinite mana. (Pearl Medallion is identical reasoning for white.) A Medallion only discounts genuinely blue/white spells cast alongside the loop, e.g., recasting Hullbreaker Horror itself. The rock that would change the math is one whose cast-plus-tap is mana-positive or whose cost a discount can actually touch — no such piece is on this board, and this resolution makes no claim beyond it.

citations.quote: Objects with no colored mana symbols in their mana costs are colorless.
an object with a mana cost of {2} is colorless
An object with no color is colorless. Colorless is not a color.

final_state.summary: The three-card version is REAL as a cast-count engine: with Hullbreaker Horror + Sol Ring + Arcane Signet and {2} to start, the alternating-bounce loop (each cast's trigger returns the OTHER rock, which is a permanent at that moment) is exactly mana-neutral per cycle — 3 mana spent, 3 produced — so the cast/storm count is unbounded within your main phase. It nets no mana, no cards, and no damage on its own, and its triggers cannot double as opponent-facing bounce without breaking the chain. Sapphire Medallion changes nothing: both rocks are colorless, so it discounts neither cast and the loop never becomes mana-positive.
